source_refs.note: Topic 1.9.1, printed pages 16-17, as printed: oxides, basic, amphoteric and acidic oxides with their equations.

blocks.text: Oxides are binary compounds formed by the reaction of oxygen with other elements. The classification of oxides is done into neutral, amphoteric and basic or acidic based on their characteristics.

A basic oxide is an oxide that when combined with water gives off an alkali. Metals react with oxygen to give basic oxides. These oxides are usually ionic in nature. Group 1 and 2 form basic oxides when react with oxygen. Examples are: Na₂O, CaO, BaO. Group 2 hydroxides solubility increases down the group so alkalinity also increases down the group.

Amphoteric oxides are oxides that can react with both acids and bases. This means they have the ability to behave as either an acid or a base, depending on the conditions. Aluminum oxide (Al₂O₃) is insoluble in water but reacts with hydrochloric acid to form aluminium chloride and water, and with sodium hydroxide to form sodium aluminate and water.

An acidic oxide is an oxide that when combined with water gives off an acid. Non-metals react with oxygen to form acidic oxides which are held together by covalent bonds. Silicon dioxide is acidic oxide as it can react with bases. Examples of acidic oxides in period 3 are: P₂O₃, P₂O₅, SO₃, SO₂
